newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: UTENOS APPEALS FOR SOLVING SHARE ROW-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: UTENOS APPEALS FOR SOLVING SHARE ROW-REPORT.

text.p: One of Lithuania's biggest brewers Utenos Beverages has requested the government and parliament solve a dispute over registering its shares with the securities commission, newspaper Lietuvos rytas said on Friday.
The company has failed to register its share capital with the securities commission for around two years due to disagreements with the government over the state's stake.
The row is over how much the state owns in the company in an argument dating back to 1993. The company has to register the shares if it wants to get a bourse listing.
"We request....that Utenos Beverages shares be registered without delay," the company said in a statement.
"The current situation does not allow Utenos Beverages to take credits, attract investments by issuing new shares or found a joint foreign capital firm," the company said.
It said it was seeing the first signs of losing its market and investments were necessary to improve the situtation.
The company's share of the local beer market has slipped recently and it said an investment of 60 to 80 million litas to upgrade production lines and marketing is necessary.
The company has also said it has a letter of intent with a potential investor but has declined to name it.

The company has been courted by both Carlsberg and Baltic Beverages Holding, owned by Finland's Hartwall and Norway's Orkla but Utenos said it cannot make an agreement with BBH due to the letter of intent.
The company's share capital stands at 22 million litas and the state owns 21.5 percent of it.
